questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.topicTitle: 2.4 Ways of Expressing Concentration of Solutions
questions.originalText: Calculate the molarity of a solution containing 4.0 g of NaOH in 500 mL of solution.
questions.explanation:
Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g/mol.
Number of moles of NaOH = 4.0 g / 40 g/mol = 0.1 mol.
Volume of solution in liters = 500 mL / 1000 = 0.5 L.
Molarity (M) = moles of solute / volume of solution (L) = 0.1 mol / 0.5 L = 0.20 M.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.originalText: What is the conjugate base of HSO4-?
questions.explanation: According to the Brønsted-Lowry theory, a conjugate base is the species formed when an acid donates a proton (H+). When HSO4- removes/donates a proton (H+), it becomes SO4 2-.
